subject: Slate stabilizer: proposed window redistribution and mitigation
messages:
From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Kyle Nguyen <kyle.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Timeline risk — eval dependencies slipping

Jordan —

Quick note from the Acme side: two items are converging that threaten our current go-live on 10/25.

1) Security team still needs the SOC2 evidence packet (requested last week) — they’ve pushed the internal review into a later cycle unless we can provide a scoped set of logs and KMS attestations by 10/19.
2) Procurement needs an updated SOW that reflects the phased acceptance path (you mentioned a canary); until they receive the redline-backed SOW and PO template, they won’t issue the PO — procurement indicated a 7–10 business day turnaround once they get the updated docs.

Given those timelines, they’re expecting a potential slip and want to see a concrete mitigation plan (MAP update + revised eval plan) by EOD Tuesday. Can you share a concrete recommendation for a re-baseline or a staged acceptance that lets Acme pilot while we finish the security packet?

Happy to hop on 30 minutes tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Lopez
Director, Platform Integrations — Acme Corp
(attachment: acme-security-reqs.pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline risk — eval dependencies slipping

Dana — thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. We should be able to avoid a full slip if we agree to a two-stage MAP:

- Stage 1 (pilot/Canary): limited dataset + reduced feature set (chat generation + reranking only), target acceptance window 10/25–10/28. This allows Acme to validate core flows and gives us production telemetry.
- Stage 2 (full eval): add streaming, function-calls, and broader traffic after SOC2 evidence is delivered; target full acceptance no earlier than 11/08.

Operational commitments from Redwood:
- Deliver a scoped SOC2 evidence packet (logs + KMS attestations) by 10/19 (we’ll include a short-gap memo describing remaining artifacts).
- Provide an updated SOW with phased acceptance language by EOD 10/13 (see SOW-redlines.pdf stub).
- Temporary mitigation: enable a lower-capacity model variant and prefix caching for pilot traffic to ensure latency SLOs while we finalize the full-serving profile.

I’ve attached a suggested MAP update and an evaluation-plan.xlsx that maps tests to acceptance gates (pilot vs full). Marissa — can you confirm procurement/PO escalation options (credits, shortened review) and any internal approvals we should line up? Karthik — can you confirm the feasibility of the temporary model variant + expected latency/cost delta?

If this plan looks acceptable I’ll send a short MAP update to Acme and request a joint sign-off on the pilot window.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
(attachment: evaluation-plan.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline risk — eval dependencies slipping

Jordan / Dana — quick procurement update from our side.

- We reviewed the SOW redlines; legal flagged three changes that lengthen review (IP carveouts + indemnity limits). I’ve attached SOW-redlines.pdf and po-checklist.docx with the minimal edits that would keep procurement moving.
- Procurement team at Acme: if Acme accepts the phased acceptance language (pilot -> full), we can accept a conditional PO with a stubbed billing line and a 15-day constraint that converts to full PO after final SOW sign-off. This would shorten the practical procurement blocker.
- On credits: we can offer a limited service credit to offset any pilot smoke-test failures that trace to environment readiness — suggest we keep this as a negotiation lever, not an initial ask.

Jordan — I’ll hold legal @ 48–72 hours for the SOW once you push the version. If we need executive sign-off I can loop in Jonas for a quick clearance.

Marissa Cole
Head, Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
(attachment: SOW-redlines.pdf; po-checklist.docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline risk — eval dependencies slipping

Jordan / team — technical readout on mitigations. Short answers then a recommended risk log entry.

- Temporary model variant: feasible. We can produce a 4-bit quantized variant that reduces GPU memory and cuts latency by ~10–20% at the cost of ~4–6% generation fidelity. This is acceptable for pilot traffic where user flows are constrained.
- Prefix/KV caching: turn on keyed prefix caching for pilot sessions — reduces token compute for repeated prompts (we estimate 18% token reduction on canonical flows).
- Canary capacity: recommend 2x smaller pool with autoscaling floor and a hard token cap per session for the pilot window. We will instrument per-route tracing and a telemetry dashboard.

Suggested risk log entry (add to MAP under "close_date_slippage"):
- id: RISK-ACME-042-001
- impact: Pilot acceptance delay could push full acceptance by 2+ weeks
- mitigation: two-stage MAP + scoped SOC2 packet + conditional PO; enable quantified temporary model variant + caching; exec escalation if legal review extends beyond 72 hours

I’ll produce the deploy config by EOD and a short runbook for toggling the variant and cache. If legal holds past 10/16 we should route to Jonas for exec clearance.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
(attachment: deploy-config-stub.yaml)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: potential slip & proposed MAP staging for ACME-2026-042

Jonas — looping you in as a heads-up and potential exec unblock.

Summary: Acme is at risk of not issuing a PO before our planned 10/25 pilot due to two outstanding items (SOC2 evidence packet and SOW redlines). Team has proposed a two-stage MAP (pilot on 10/25 with limited feature set; full eval by 11/08). Technical mitigations and a temporary model variant are ready. Marissa is holding legal for 48–72 hours on the SOW.

Ask: if legal pushes past 10/16 or procurement pushes on PO timing, please advise whether we should:
- escalate for a one-time executive exception to accept a conditional PO on stubbed billing (preferred), or
- authorize a short-term credit/financial concession to accelerate procurement sign-off.

I’ve attached the eval plan and SOW redlines; Acme asked for a formal MAP update by EOD 10/13 — we met that; we now need to lock procurement and SOC2 delivery windows to avoid a full slip.

Happy to jump on a 15-minute call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
(attachments: evaluation-plan.xlsx, SOW-redlines.pdf)
